sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h11 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i08, caller. Medium target, Hard welcome (user,
  2026-10-10: no Easy slot). Platform: rev 0 Run 1 "Between levels", Low 0/5 · Medium 5/5 (## Platform
  validation): the method trap held the low model and cost the medium model nothing. Rev 1 is the one
  focused repair: the trap is kept, and the order side now needs three derived arrival dates, each set
  against a different order's printed deadline. Measured result for rev 1 pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 4 L30 (rule: "received by June 26, 2026"), L33-34 and L39 (portal only, electronic).
  Doc 5 L25, L27: June order issued June 21, comments on or before July 10. Doc 6 L25, L27: July order
  issued July 13, comments on or before July 31. Doc 7 L25, L28: August order issued August 12, comments on
  or before September 1. Nineteen days after issue: July 10 (the June order's last day, counts), August 1
  (a day after the July order's deadline, does not count), August 31 (a day before the August order's
  deadline, counts). Rule: 30 letters out, 18 portal comments of June 25 in. 18 + 22 + 22 = 62.
- Universe: five groups, 114 comments in all (30 + 18 + 22 x 3); 62 accepted, 52 not (30 + 22).
- Why the three orders differ: each deadline is 15 days after Federal Register publication, and the
  notices appeared 4, 3 and 5 days after issue (June 25, July 16, August 17), so the deadlines fall 19, 18
  and 20 days after issue. The same 19-day lag is therefore just in time, a day late and a day early.
- Necessity: Doc 4 is the only document with the rule's portal-only method and June 26 date. Doc 5 is the
  only document with the June order's deadline (July 10); Doc 6 and Doc 7 give that order only "a 15-day
  comment period", under which a batch 19 days after issue is late (40 instead of 62). Doc 7 is the only
  document with the August order's deadline and the only one that prints that order at all. Doc 6 is the
  only document with the July order's deadline, the fact that rules its batch out; because Doc 7's "15-day
  comment period" for that order points the same way, a solver without Doc 6 could reach the same count by
  the label, so Doc 6 is entered as an Exclusion / condition source with a note rather than as an answer
  component. The wording states no rule, no deadline and no issue date.
- Selected-lever checks (Python, 2026-10-10): gold 18 + 22 + 22 = 62. Orders' mail rule carried to the rule:
  92. All three order batches counted (one order worked out and the others assumed alike): 84; with the
  letters: 114. The 15-day label instead of the printed deadlines (no order batch counts): 18. June batch
  dropped by a one-day slip: 40. Offsets checked for 15 to 21 days: 19 is the only lag at which the three
  orders split two ways with no batch more than a day from its deadline.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope, misapplies a rule or premise) -> 92, the
  orders' mail rule applied to the interim rule. Measured on rev 0 Run 1: all five low attempts counted the
  30 letters (answer 91 there; low attempt 1 wrote "Allowed methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal or mail" for
  the rule, another gave it the EOIR rule's postmark wording). Considered and not declared, nothing observed
  yet: treating the three orders alike (84) and the 15-day label (18). Re-declare from rev 1's observed wrong
  answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: Python datetime 2026-10-10: June 21 plus 19 days is July 10 (on the deadline);
  July 13 plus 19 days is August 1 (after July 31); August 12 plus 19 days is August 31 (before September 1).
  18 + 22 = 40; 40 + 22 = 62. Convention: elapsed days, the ordinary meaning of "N days after".
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 62, the three arrival dates or the scenario's counts.
  Shortest route: the rule's DATES and ADDRESSES, then each order's issue date and DATES line, three date
  additions, one sum.
- Precision/readings: "issued" is the date each SUMMARY gives ("This Order was issued on ..."). Doc 6's
  signature block is dated July 14; taking that date moves the July batch to August 2, still late, so the
  count does not change. "19 days after" is the issue date plus 19; counting the issue day as day one would
  put the July batch on July 31 and give 84, which is not what "after" means. "On or before July 10"
  includes July 10. "Its June, July and August Ebola entry orders" are the orders issued June 21, July 13
  and August 12; the May orders are not in question. "Letters" are mailed paper comments. Labelling
  instructions are outside "method and timing".
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md coverage lines).
- Style/set review: 52 words, one ask. No other live question in the bundle.
- Scenario numbers: 30, 18, 22, 25 and 19 are printed in digits in Doc 5 (19 at character 19,092, the
  deepest; the form has been seen to read to 19,581), so its number check has a document for each.
- Revision history: rev 1 (2026-10-10) answers difficulty Run 1 on rev 0 (Version b8861d, "Between
  levels"; Feedback log; index F7). Changed: the order side of the scenario (the 21 order letters and the
  July 10 pair replaced by one batch per order, each 19 days after issue), the gold (61 to 62), Doc 6 and
  Doc 7 added, Steps 2-12, evidence, tags (Temporal alignment added). Unchanged: the rule side (30 letters,
  18 portal comments, June 25), the closing question, the failure-mode pair. A first draft of rev 1 with
  explicit dates (July 10, 12, 30, August 5 on "the order then in force", snapshot b65e272d...) was set
  aside before hand-over: it repeated the order-in-force lookup the easier solver had already cleared five
  times on this bundle. If rev 1 is again Between levels with the medium model at 4 or 5 of 5, the hook has
  no Medium form and that is reported; if the medium model falls to 0 of 5, the High result decides (Hard is
  an open tier).
- Coach suggestions on rev 0, checked against the text: (1) relative descriptions instead of the explicit
  dates: adopted in substance for the order side (the question now gives a lag, not dates). (2) asking which
  requirement each failing group broke: not adopted, it makes two asks and a long answer.
- Warnings answered: floor run recorded at hand-over (rev 1).

sections.question: On June 25, 2026, CDC received 30 letters and 18 portal comments on its interim quarantine rule. It also received 22 portal comments on each of its June, July and August Ebola entry orders, each batch arriving 19 days after that order was issued. How many met CDC's requirements on method and timing?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, DATES and ADDRESSES): comments on the interim final rule must be received by June 26, 2026. They may be submitted by one method only, the Federal eRulemaking Portal, and all comments must be submitted electronically.

Step 2. Application (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the 30 letters on the rule were not submitted electronically, so they do not meet the rule's method requirement. The 18 portal comments on the rule arrived on June 25, before June 26, and count.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, SUMMARY and DATES): the June order was issued on June 21, 2026, and written comments on it must be received on or before July 10, 2026.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): June has 30 days, so the days of June left after June 21 are 30 - 21 = 9.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): the rest of the 19 days fall in July: 19 - 9 = 10. That batch arrived on July 10, the last day allowed, so its 22 comments count.

Step 6. Source input (Doc 6, SUMMARY and DATES): the July order was issued on July 13, 2026, and written comments on it must be received on or before July 31, 2026.

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): July has 31 days, so the days of July left after July 13 are 31 - 13 = 18.

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): the rest of the 19 days fall in August: 19 - 18 = 1. That batch arrived on August 1, after July 31, so its 22 comments do not count.

Step 9. Source input (Doc 7, SUMMARY and DATES): the August order was issued on August 12, 2026, and written comments on it must be received on or before September 1, 2026.

Step 10. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 7): the day of August on which that batch arrived: 12 + 19 = 31. August 31 is before September 1, so its 22 comments count.

Step 11. Calculation (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the rule's timely portal comments plus the June order's batch: 18 + 22 = 40.

Step 12. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 7): adding the August order's batch: 40 + 22 = 62.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 5's, Doc 6's and Doc 7's orders accept mailed comments, but Doc 4's interim rule takes comments only through the portal. Carrying the orders' mail rule to the rule counts its 30 letters: 92. The rule's own terms give 62.
